summary.text: A 65-year-old man with heavy tobacco use and no known comorbidities was transferred with persistent fever, rapidly progressive kidney dysfunction and dyspnea after a 2-month history of weakness, fatigue, weight loss, right-sided hearing loss and leg hypoesthesia. Admission creatinine was 5.8 mg/dL and CRP 121 mg/L; infectious workup was negative and p-ANCA with anti-MPO 95.1 IU/L was positive.

Kidney biopsy showed pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis; CT showed a UIP pattern and ENT involvement; troponin was elevated without chest pain with LVEF 20% and myocarditis on cardiac MRI, and coronary angiography excluded significant coronary disease. Sensory deficits suggested peripheral neuropathy. Findings were consistent with MPO-AAV with BVAS 41.

Treatment included methylprednisolone, prednisolone, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, seven plasma exchange sessions and avacopan 30 mg twice daily started 15 days after starting immunosuppression. At 1 month creatinine was 5.3 mg/dL without hemodialysis and LVEF 50%; at 3 months creatinine was 3.9 mg/dL and systolic function normalized; clinical remission was reached by 6 months with radiologic ILD improvement, rituximab maintenance and continued avacopan, with one serious urinary tract infection.

summary.text: A 68-year-old man with hypertension, coronary artery disease, HFrEF, treated atrial flutter and psoriasis presented to the emergency department with acute kidney injury and progressive scrotal swelling over 10 days after a month of weakness, weight loss and arthralgias; a 10-day course of oral ciprofloxacin gave no improvement. Admission creatinine was 5.3 mg/dL with CRP 160 mg/L and scrotal ultrasonography consistent with acute epididymo-orchitis.

Urethral secretions were positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and blood cultures and viral serologies were negative; ceftriaxone and levofloxacin gave no improvement. By day 7 creatinine peaked at 7.3 mg/dL; anti-PR3 antibodies were 121.6 U/mL and kidney biopsy showed crescentic glomerulonephritis, leading to a diagnosis of PR3-AAV with kidney involvement and epididymo-orchitis, BVAS 15.

Treatment comprised methylprednisolone pulses from day 7 then oral methylprednisolone, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, seven plasma exchange sessions, intermittent hemodialysis and avacopan 30 mg twice daily started 15 days after starting immunosuppression. Creatinine improved to 2.3, 2.1 and 1.7 mg/dL at 1, 3 and 6 months, epididymo-orchitis resolved within 1 month, two leukopenia episodes resolved after temporary avacopan discontinuation, and no serious infection occurred.
